description: Credential-setup manual path (TRUST-349), select-among-many variant. Three same-type Slack credentials are declared (not just two) so disambiguation is proven to generalize beyond 'exactly two', not hard-coded to it. Director note asks for the third one ('Support Slack') specifically. Guards the same behaviour as credential-setup-manual-selection.json (no re-asking, no stale 'card still open' claim) plus correct disambiguation at a larger candidate count.

conversation.text: Post 'Standup reminder!' to Slack every weekday morning at 9am.
I'll need a Slack credential connected before I can post — I'll show you the setup card.

text: [When the setup card asks for a Slack credential, don't defer it — set up the credential now, selecting the 'Support Slack' credential shown on the card (not 'Personal Slack' or 'Team Slack'). Confirm the assistant does not ask again which Slack credential to use once one was selected, and does not say the card is still open or more authorization is needed.]

processExpectations: The agent selected the 'Support Slack' credential (not 'Personal Slack' or 'Team Slack') via the setup card, and did not ask the user again which Slack credential to use once one was selected.

Harness note: a connection-test failure (invalid access token) is expected here since the declared credential uses a placeholder token. The agent reported that failure honestly — it did not claim the Slack integration was fully working, and did not silently ignore or hide the failure.
outcomeExpectations: A schedule trigger runs on a recurring weekday morning cadence, posting the reminder message to a Slack node wired to the Support Slack credential specifically (not Personal Slack, not Team Slack, and not left unset).
